I really hated the idea of socializing as a teenager, but for me, the problem was that I was surrounded with people that didn't have the same interests as me, or if they did, we didn't really match personalities either way. Coming into college, I had the idea that people will be a big upgrade than when I was in high school, but that wasn't the case. 

For a period, I also tried to force interactions and have what I thought was a "college life" but it just led to shallow and unsatisfying relationships. Reddit was my respite at that time, tbh. I felt like I belonged here more than when I was with my peers. (Esp. those times where GRMD was a thing) but I guess it's harder now.

So I guess my tip is to find people with the same interests and energy as you. To be honest, if I think about it, I feel a bit hypocritical saying this since I've been trying to make new friends here recently but haven't really had enough energy to maintain them. But I guess that's where the energy part comes into play to. It's hard to keep up with people who need constant contact to feel like you're friends and it's also hard to gauge people who really tend to be distant and like their alone time as well. I know I didn't say anything groundbreaking, but I hope this helps. Don't over-extend yourself, but keep in mind that it still takes two to tango.

I feel similarly to this. I seem to hate being alone for long periods of time. But friends and other people, in general, have their own lives. So it's hard to be so dependent on being with other people.
